newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Sept jobless rate surges to 9.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Sept jobless rate surges to 9.9 pct.

text.p: Canada's unemployment rate jumped 0.5 percent to an unexpectedly high 9.9 percent in September as the economy lost 47,000 jobs, Statistics Canada said on Friday.
The government agency said full-time employment fell by 86,000, wiping out the 72,000-job gain in August and cutting the year's total gains in half. Part-time employment rose by 39,000 in September.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast the unemployment rate would drop to 9.3 percent and employment grow by 37,000 in Statistics Canada said three-quarters of the overall job
decline occurred in Ontario. Employment in Canada's richest province fell by 35,000, partly offsetting the 82,000 jobs created in the two previous months.

The agency said all the job losses in September were in the service industries, which lost 48,000 jobs in the month. A drop of 70,000 in community, business and personal services wiped out all the employment gains so far this year, the agency said.
Employment rose by 20,000 in finance, insurance and real estate.

The total number of jobs created so far this year fell to 106,000 in September from 153,000 in August. Statistics Canada said employment in manufacturing industries has risen by a net 94,000 since the beginning of the year, after a total of 104,000 jobs had been created.

Employment in Quebec, which lost 41,000 jobs in June and 35,000 jobs in July before gaining 41,000 jobs in August, remained little changed in September. The French-speaking province has lost 26,000 jobs since December 1995, Statistics Canada said.
